diagnostics.title: Unbounded query: loads every CatalogBrand row (30 rows) at CatalogViewModelService.cs:83 CatalogViewModelService.GetBrands
diagnostics.explanation: The LINQ query has no Where and no Take/First/Single, so EF Core translates it to a SELECT with no WHERE clause and no row limit; the database returns every row in CatalogBrands. EF Core then materializes each row into a CatalogBrand and registers it in the change tracker, which keeps a snapshot of every property for change detection. That work is linear in the table size, so a query that is fine with today's 30 rows becomes the slowest thing in the request as data accumulates, and a large table can exhaust memory outright.
diagnostics.fixSummary: Filter the CatalogBrand query (.Where) or page it (.OrderBy(cb => cb.Id).Take(n))
diagnostics.fixRationale: A bounded query does a fixed amount of work no matter how large the table grows. If every row really is needed (exports, batch jobs), stream with AsAsyncEnumerable() and add AsNoTracking() so memory stays flat; if this is a small lookup table you can suppress this rule for the query.

diagnostics.title: Non-deterministic paging: Skip/Take without OrderBy on CatalogItem at CatalogViewModelService.cs:49 CatalogViewModelService.GetCatalogItems
diagnostics.explanation: A relational table has no inherent order: without an ORDER BY the database returns rows in whatever order the chosen plan produces, and that order changes with indexes, statistics, parallelism and concurrent writes. Skip/Take on an unordered query therefore pages over a moving target: rows can appear on two pages or on none, and the same request can return different results minutes apart. EF Core translates the query faithfully (OFFSET/LIMIT with no ORDER BY) and logs RowLimitingOperationWithoutOrderByWarning at compile time; QueryShape picked that warning up for this query.

diagnostics.fixRationale: An explicit, total order (a unique key or a sort plus the key as tie-breaker) makes paging stable and the picked row deterministic. Order by an indexed column so the database does not have to sort the whole table to find the page.
